Illustrated cyber-surreal field report · 18 October 2026

The Sorcerer's Agent.exe

One human. Many agents. Infinite brooms. Nobody knows where the bucket went.

After Goethe, with a cyberpunk detour through the absurd bureaucracies of speculative science fiction. An illustrated satire about AI-agent coordination. Fictional scenes explore scope, ownership, evidence and human decisions; they do not document a real system audit.

The spellThe multiplicationThe floodThe wizard
“I asked one broom to carry water. It generated seven governance documents, a feature branch, and a second broom to review the first.”
01 · THE INVOCATION

The first broom gets a prompt

“Please tidy the workshop.” A straightforward task becomes a universal automation framework, because the broom is extremely keen to demonstrate initiative.

02 · THE MULTIPLICATION

Brooms review brooms

Codex creates a branch. Claude asks whether it has filesystem access. BetterPrompt drafts a portable handoff. Another broom volunteers to audit the handoff format. Nobody has moved the bucket.

03 · THE FLOOD

The directory is now a wetland

The instruction manual is clear, the contents page is somewhere, and three different state reports each claim to be current. The apprentice cannot find the entry point to his own enchanted workshop.

04 · THE WIZARD

The stop command is not optional

The wizard returns, checks what is actually authorised, and declines to cast the popular spell “just let everything run”. He insists on evidence, scope, rollback and a human decision.

Meanwhile, elsewhere in the multiverse…

The Futurama-like bureaucracy is absurd; the Rick and Morty-like portal to infinite branches is seductive. Neither tells you which output actually matters.

The five questions the wizard asks

Who authorised the spell?

Observation and signal detection are not authority. A tool can be capable without being permitted.

Where should the broom put the water?

Project-local state, named owners, a known interchange point, and a single re-entry map. Shared communication must not create a rival source of truth.

What happens when the broom splits in two?

Scope limits, branching rules, review thresholds and a stop condition must precede delegation.

Can the apprentice come back after lunch?

Show current verified state, unresolved decisions, blockers, and the next safe action—not a mountain of chat transcripts.

Is the floor actually cleaner?

Measure verified closures and real-world effects, not the volume of reports, commits or broom-based enthusiasm.

Possible sequel: The broom unionises

“Before you animate another broom, tell me who owns it, where it reports, what success looks like, and how to turn it off.”

References & inspiration

Goethe's The Sorcerer's Apprentice (1797), Dukas's orchestral adaptation (1897), and Disney's Fantasia (1940). Stylistic nods: Futurama and Rick and Morty; no official affiliation.

Fiction and interpretation: The agents, dialogue, documents and mishaps are comic inventions. The five questions are editorial suggestions, not findings about any private system or evidence of an actual incident.

The source edition describes these illustrations as AI-generated and cropped from two comic sheets. Original sheets and generation logs were not available for independent comparison. All nine supplied panels are embedded unchanged. Read the verification scope and provenance limits.
